// EVOLVE-BLOCK-START
// HYPOTHESIS-1: Hybrid introsort with median-of-three pivot, insertion sort for small arrays, and heap sort fallback will improve performance on adversarial inputs
// MECHANISM-1: Median-of-three avoids worst-case O(n^2) on sorted data; insertion sort is fast for small n; depth limit prevents stack overflow

// HYPOTHESIS-2: Detecting nearly-sorted runs via adjacent inversions (O(n) check) and using insertion sort will improve adaptability across diverse data patterns
// MECHANISM-2: Nearly-sorted data has few adjacent inversions so insertion sort is O(n); this adapts behavior to input characteristics with minimal overhead
// EXPECT-2: adaptability_score > 0.995

pub fn adaptive_sort<T: Ord + Clone>(arr: &mut [T]) {
    let len = arr.len();
    if len <= 1 { return; }
    if len <= 32 { insertion_sort(arr); return; }
    // O(n) near-sorted check: count adjacent inversions
    let mut adj_inv = 0usize;
    for i in 0..len - 1 {
        if arr[i] > arr[i + 1] { adj_inv += 1; }
    }
    if adj_inv <= len / 8 {
        insertion_sort(arr);
        return;
    }
    let max_depth = (2.0 * (len as f64).log2()) as usize;
    introsort(arr, max_depth);
}

fn introsort<T: Ord + Clone>(arr: &mut [T], depth: usize) {
    let len = arr.len();
    if len <= 16 { insertion_sort(arr); return; }
    if depth == 0 { heap_sort(arr); return; }
    let pi = partition_mo3(arr);
    let (left, right) = arr.split_at_mut(pi);
    introsort(left, depth - 1);
    introsort(&mut right[1..], depth - 1);
}

fn partition_mo3<T: Ord + Clone>(arr: &mut [T]) -> usize {
    let len = arr.len();
    let mid = len / 2;
    let last = len - 1;
    // Median-of-three pivot selection
    if arr[0] > arr[mid] { arr.swap(0, mid); }
    if arr[0] > arr[last] { arr.swap(0, last); }
    if arr[mid] > arr[last] { arr.swap(mid, last); }
    arr.swap(mid, last - 1);
    let pivot = arr[last - 1].clone();
    let mut i = 1usize;
    let mut j = last - 2;
    loop {
        while arr[i] < pivot { i += 1; }
        while j > 0 && arr[j] > pivot { j -= 1; }
        if i >= j { break; }
        arr.swap(i, j);
        i += 1; j -= 1;
    }
    arr.swap(i, last - 1);
    i
}

fn heap_sort<T: Ord>(arr: &mut [T]) {
    let len = arr.len();
    for i in (0..len / 2).rev() { sift_down(arr, i, len); }
    for i in (1..len).rev() {
        arr.swap(0, i);
        sift_down(arr, 0, i);
    }
}

fn sift_down<T: Ord>(arr: &mut [T], mut root: usize, end: usize) {
    loop {
        let mut child = 2 * root + 1;
        if child >= end { break; }
        if child + 1 < end && arr[child] < arr[child + 1] { child += 1; }
        if arr[root] >= arr[child] { break; }
        arr.swap(root, child);
        root = child;
    }
}

fn insertion_sort<T: Ord>(arr: &mut [T]) {
    for i in 1..arr.len() {
        let mut j = i;
        while j > 0 && arr[j - 1] > arr[j] {
            arr.swap(j, j - 1);
            j -= 1;
        }
    }
}

fn introsort<T: Ord>(mut arr: &mut [T], mut depth: usize) {
    loop {
        let len = arr.len();
        if len <= 16 { insertion_sort(arr); return; }
        if depth == 0 { heap_sort(arr); return; }
        depth -= 1;

        let pi = partition_mo3(arr);
        let (left, right) = arr.split_at_mut(pi);

        // Recurse into smaller side; iterate on larger to reduce stack usage.
        if left.len() < right.len() - 1 {
            introsort(left, depth);
            arr = &mut right[1..];
        } else {
            introsort(&mut right[1..], depth);
            arr = left;
        }
    }
